prediction.likelyOutcome: Caton has a genuine, textually supported claim that the Section 1(b) conditions had already failed (helped significantly by the Trust's own fifth-amendment recital), but the Trust's argument that no obligation ripened absent exercise of the option is a serious competing reading, and the parties' continued extensions after the recital plus the 'material adversity' dispute over the encroachment create real factual issues likely to survive summary judgment and go to trial. Expected recovery, probability-weighted, lands well below the full $442,885.50 demand, with the documented $314,000 option-consideration component carrying materially better odds than the deposition-only $128,885.50 expense component.

issues.label: Core liability: Section 9(a) liquidated-damages trigger without exercise (option consideration component)
Materiality of the Overlook adverse-possession encroachment under Section 1(b)(iv)'s exception

outcome.description: The circuit court granted Caton summary judgment on a futility theory and awarded him $442,885.50 in damages (the full amount of his demand) plus $96,329.00 in attorneys' fees. The Court of Appeals of Virginia affirmed that the agreement required Caton to exercise the option, but reversed the summary judgment award of damages and fees because futility was not established as a matter of law, and remanded for further proceedings.
outcome.finalNote: Summary judgment reversed and remanded; no final figure yet.
